problem.title: Minimum Number of Swaps to Make the String Balanced

approaches.title: Single-pass imbalance counting
approaches.summary: Scan the string once while tracking bracket balance, then compute the swaps from the unmatched closing brackets or maximum prefix deficit. Revisions 2 and 3 refine the scan and express the same underlying strategy differently.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Count unmatched closing brackets in a character scan and return half rounded up.

revisions.commitComment: use u32 for built in ceiling div & faster iter w/ as_bytes()
revisions.rawCommitSubject: rust 1963: use u32 for built in ceiling div & faster iter w/ as_bytes()
revisions.diffFromPreviousRelevantRevision:
diff --git a/rust/src/bin/1963_minimum_number_of_swaps_to_make_the_string_balanced.rs b/rust/src/bin/1963_minimum_number_of_swaps_to_make_the_string_balanced.rs
index fdee1bf..4ed6798 100644
--- a/rust/src/bin/1963_minimum_number_of_swaps_to_make_the_string_balanced.rs
+++ b/rust/src/bin/1963_minimum_number_of_swaps_to_make_the_string_balanced.rs
@@ -1,12 +1,14 @@
 impl Solution {
     pub fn min_swaps(s: String) -> i32 {
-        let (_, errors) = s.chars().fold((0, 0), |(open, errors), c| match c {
-            '(' => (open + 1, errors),
-            _ if open > 0 => (open - 1, errors),
-            _ => (open, errors + 1),
-        });
-
-        (errors + 1) / 2
+        s.as_bytes()
+            .iter()
+            .fold((0, 0_u32), |(open, errors), b| match b {
+                b'[' => (open + 1, errors),
+                _ if open > 0 => (open - 1, errors),
+                _ => (open, errors + 1),
+            })
+            .1
+            .div_ceil(2) as i32
     }
 }
revisions.shortChangeSummary: Use byte iteration and `div_ceil` while retaining the unmatched-closing count.

revisions.commitComment: since open = close, max_diff = total errors. Reducing branching

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Track the minimum prefix balance and derive the swap count from the maximum deficit.

approaches.title: Explicitly swap mismatched brackets
approaches.summary: Scan from the left and, whenever a closing bracket cannot be matched, swap it with an opening bracket found from the right. Count each performed swap.

revisions.shortChangeSummary: Replace deficit counting with a two-pointer simulation that swaps each unmatched closing bracket with a right-side opening bracket.
